ing: such as snapper, cut in chunks
st: Rub the fish with the lime juice and [[1 tsp]] salt. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat the palm oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions and garlic for [[6 minutes]] until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until they break down.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water, add the whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the okra if using, then slide in the fish. Simmer gently for 15 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Do not stir much.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it with [[4 cups]] water and a pinch of salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes.
Remove the chili. Serve the fish and palm oil broth over the rice.

ing: finely minced, or 2 tsp chili flakes
st: Blend or mash the onion, garlic, chilies, lime juice, [[0.25 cup]] oil, paprika, [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper into a wet paste.
Cut a few slashes in the chicken skin and rub the paste all over, working it into the cuts.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least [[3 hours]], or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium or the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lift the chicken out of the marinade and shake off excess pieces of onion.
Cook, turning every 10 minutes and brushing with leftover marinade for the first half only, for about 45 minutes.
Check that the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C) and the skin is browned and charred in spots.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with rice or fries.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt. Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
Cook the onions and garlic in the same pot for [[5 minutes]], then stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes for 8 minutes.
Return the chicken with [[3 cups]] water, the chili and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it with [[4 cups]] water and a pinch of salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes.
Remove the chili and serve the stew over the rice.
Blend the tomatoes, chopped bell pepper, one onion, garlic and half the chili until smooth.
Season the fish with [[1 tsp]] salt. Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot and fry the fish 2 minutes per side. Set aside.
In the same oil, cook the sliced onion for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 3 minutes.
Pour in the blended sauce and cook for 15 minutes, stirring, until it has thickened and reduced.
Add [[4 cups]] water, the thyme, carrots, the rest of the chili (whole) and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Lay the fish on top, cover and steam for 10 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fluff gently, remove the chili and serve.
Scrub the oysters under cold running water. Throw away any that are open and do not close when tapped.
Heat a grill to high, or heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Mix the melted butter, garlic, herbs and half the minced chili in a small bowl.
Place the oysters cupped side down on the grill, directly over the heat.
Grill for 4 to 6 minutes until the shells pop open a little and the juices bubble.
Carefully remove them with tongs. Wear a glove or hold with a towel and twist open with an oyster knife or sturdy blade, keeping the liquid in the shell.
Spoon over the garlic butter and remaining chili. Squeeze lime juice on top and eat right away.
